review: Read complete Desktop Updates and Device Check components, native runtime provider, personal availability helper, three panel suites and unchanged runtime suite. Reviewed the previously exported account-policy dependency and exact profile-revision mechanism. First-party UI and synthetic bridge/HTTP fixtures only.

Device Check distinguishes ordinary personal Full Harness setup from saved read-only private tunnels. Developer tunnel configuration and full-scope controls remain separate. Local status explicitly does not prove remote exact-task MCP availability.

Integrated-world selection uses the native folder picker and typed state parser. The renderer grants no game action, starts no Minecraft process, and ordinary users do not receive developer dedicated-server controls.

The new profile-revision wrapper clears prior-account observations, drafts, busy state and pending UI callbacks by remounting the internal panel. Native operation authorization is not replaced and an already-started native operation is not canceled by this UI reset.

Private update guidance now describes recovery under an existing owner-approved setup contract after account, developer grant, trust and package checks. Neither updating nor this guidance renews a game grant. Public download/install buttons remain explicit native bridge actions.

Runtime provider changes are optional TypeScript bridge declarations for existing personal setup, integrated-world selection, isolated speech, budgets, storage and publishing APIs. Declaring a method is not evidence of installed availability or authority. Origin-bound handshake implementation is unchanged.

Existing Device Check fixture C:/Users/owner/AppData/Roaming/.minecraft is a literal mock return, not a filesystem read. New account-isolation tests use C:/Games/FixtureMinecraft and synthetic profile IDs. No real account payload or local file contents are exported.
The new regression fixture now supplies the required getRuntimeSnapshot bridge member; this is a type-shape correction after the historical 17-test receipt, with no production behavior change.
limits: Private unfrozen source candidate only; no publication or native restart.
Mocked UI tests do not verify signed installation/updating, persisted native world selection, host-account isolation or live MCP enrollment.
The profile-isolation production fix and its new tests are newer than running R380.
Native server/preload admission, shared contracts and other client helpers remain separate dependencies; the preview is not a standalone app.
Three-person voice, GPT Live game context, Agent API funding and the coordinated signed public release remain separately open.
